To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the block-wise AD-GBS is an efficient algorithm for multiple-block convex programming, and it can be further improved in two ways, one of which is to iteratively calculate the step sizes and the other is to linearize the subproblems, and the resulting algorithms are suitable for a centralized distributed-computing system to handle big-data problems.

the block-wise alternating direction method of multipliers with Gaussian back substitution can be extended for the multiple-block separable convex minimization model and that this extended version can be further refined by using the iteratively calculated step size and linearized subproblem, which can be applied to handle big data with high efficiency and scalability.

a splitting method for the t-block regouped multiple-block convex program can be designed and analyzed based on the ADMM- GB S with Gaussian back substitution, and that this splitting method can be implemented for the big-data scenario where the number of blocks is huge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an efficient algorithm for the big-data scenario, and the new algorithm and its refined versions can be applied to solve many concrete big-data applications.
the design and convergence analysis of an efficient algorithm for the multiple-block linearly constrained convex programming with a separable and non-smooth objective function.
a new splitting algorithm for a specific big-data model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the block-wise ADM M-GBS with Gaussian back substitution for multiple-block convex programming with big data is a promising algorithmic tool for big data.

the new algorithm and its refined versions are the most efficient and scalable algorithms in the literature when m is huge and the functions in the original objective are separable with respect to different variables.

we propose a new algorithm, called the block-wise AD-GBS with further decomposition (BD-GBS), to solve the m-block regrouped multiple-block convex programming model, and establish its convergence and worst-case iteration complexity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an efficient algorithm for the big-data convex programming with a separable and linearly constrained objective.
we have designed a novel algorithm for the particular big data scenario and have established the convergence and complexity of the new algorithm.

we propose an algorithm for solving the linearly constrained multiple-block convex minimization problem with a huge number of blocks, where each block has only a handleable number of functions and variables; we prove its convergence; and we establish its worst-case iteration complexity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the big-data convex minimization with m functions and m variables, the block-wise AD- MM-GBS is a promising method to handle the model when m is huge, and the block-wise splitting method can be further refined by further splitting the subproblems of the block-wise splitting algorithm.

the block-wise alternating direction method of multipliers with Gaussian back substitution can be a good candidate for the multiple-block convex programming problem with a separable and linearly constrained objective function.

the block-wise ADM-GBS with further decompositions and the proposed splitting version can be very efficient for the particular big- data scenario where the objective function is the sum of many separable functions with no coupled variables and the number of these functions is huge.
